task: Zillow state-level 8 house-type CAGR (2010-12-31 -> 2019-12-31) and within-state growth-rate disparity, Top5 output

method.data_loading: Read 8 Zillow state-level CSV files (State_Zhvi_{1bedroom,2bedroom,3bedroom,4bedroom,5BedroomOrMore,AllHomes,Condominum,SingleFamilyResidence}.csv) with pandas, usecols=['RegionName','RegionType','StateName','2010-12-31','2019-12-31']. Verified by header scan that both target date columns exist in every file at identical positions (0-based index 185 and 293 respectively, 297 cols total, 291 monthly date columns 1996-01..2020-03).
method.property_type_mapping: Derived from file names: 1 bedroom / 2 bedroom / 3 bedroom / 4 bedroom / 5 bedroom or more / All homes / Condominium / Single family residence (property type is not a column in the source data).
method.cagr: cagr = (value_2019_12_31 / value_2010_12_31)^(1/9) - 1, exponent 9 = annual intervals 2011..2019; applied only where both values > 0.
method.disparity: For each of the 51 regions (50 states + District of Columbia): growth_rate_diff = max(cagr over 8 types) - min(cagr over 8 types); sorted descending (ties by region_name asc), rank 1..51.
method.unit_convention: growth_rate_diff stored as decimal CAGR in state_cagr_disparity.csv, reported as percentage points (x100, 4 dp) in top5_cagr_disparity.csv to match the upstream result convention.
method.top5_selection: First 5 rows after descending sort on growth_rate_diff.

validation.negative_cagr_note: Only Connecticut shows a slight nominal decline in one property type over the period.

spot_checks.note: [value_2010_12_31, value_2019_12_31, recomputed cagr]; all match the pipeline output.

validation.reproduces_upstream_artifact: Independent recomputation from the raw CSVs reproduced the existing top5_cagr_disparity.csv byte-for-byte in content (same 5 regions and same 4-dp values).

key_intermediate_results.drivers: In Florida, Nevada and Georgia the fastest-growing type is 1 bedroom and the slowest is 5 bedroom or more; in District of Columbia and Kansas the extremes are 1 bedroom vs 3/4 bedroom, i.e. small vs large unit size drives the dispersion rather than condominium vs single-family.

limitations: District of Columbia included although not a state (as in Zillow's state files).
CAGR endpoints are single monthly observations (2010-12-31, 2019-12-31), so results are sensitive to endpoint noise.
